prompt: Single continuous shot, no scene cuts, real-time speed, vintage film camera. The two men in shirtsleeves and braces crouch at the vault door, holding the blowtorch flame steady against the steel. As the steel heats, real temper colours bloom outward from the white-hot point: straw yellow, bronze, purple, deep blue, in rings that spread slowly across the polished round door like oil on water. Sparks pour from the cut and skitter across the wet floor, each one trailing a short streak of orange light. The guard on the left holds his tommy gun upright, muzzle pointed straight at the ceiling, and turns his head slowly to watch the dark doorway. Camera locked off for five seconds, then tilts down and pushes low along the wet floor into the bouncing sparks, so the frame becomes scattered points of light on black. Sound: the hiss of the torch, sparks hitting concrete. No dialogue, no on-screen text.
